business_model.claim: Hafnia is an international shipping company that provides seaborne transportation of refined oil, other petroleum products, and certain chemical products using a fleet of LR2, LR1, MR, Handy, and Specialised tankers.
quotes: We are an international shipping company providing seaborne transportation of refined oil, other petroleum products and certain chemical products.

business_model.claim: Hafnia's customers are leading international oil companies, national oil companies, major chemical companies, and trading and utility companies.
quotes: We are one of the world's largest operators of chemical and product tankers and provide transportation of oil and oil products to leading international oil companies and national oil companies, major chemical companies, as well as trading and utility companies.

business_model.basis: stated in P3 (Item 5, How We Evaluate Our Operations)
business_model.claim: The company's reporting segments are LR2 tankers, LR1 tankers, MR tankers, and Handy tankers; Chemical-MR and Chemical-Handy vessels are grouped under the MR and Handy segments respectively.
quotes: We manage our business through the following operating and reporting segments:

Previously, we reported on "Chemical-MR" vessels and "Chemical-Handy" vessels as separate segments, however we have now grouped "Chemical-MR" and "Chemical-Handy" vessels under the MR segment and the Handy segment, respectively.

business_model.claim: Revenue primarily consists of voyage charter and time charter income; as at December 31, 2025, 85 of the Hafnia Vessels and TC Vessels operated in the Pools or on spot charters outside the Pools, and 23 were on time charter-out agreements.
quotes: Revenue primarily consists of revenue from voyage charters and time charters.

As at December 31, 2025, 85 of our Hafnia Vessels and TC Vessels were operating in the Pools or on spot charters outside the Pools and 23 were operating on time charter-out agreements outside of the Pools.

business_model.claim: Hafnia operates nine pools (LR2, LR1, Panamax, MR, Handy, Chemical-MR, Chemical-Handy, and Small and City Pools collectively called the Specialised Pool) through which the majority of its Hafnia Vessels and TC Vessels are employed on voyage charters and time charters with profit sharing among pool participants.
quotes: We operate the following nine pools that we refer to collectively as the Pools: LR2 Pool, LR1 Pool, Panamax Pool, MR Pool, Handy Pool, Chemical-MR Pool, Chemical-Handy Pool and Small and City Pools, which are collectively referred to as the Specialised Pool.
The majority of our Hafnia Vessels and TC Vessels are employed on voyage charters and time charters through our Pools, whereby earnings are subject to profit sharing with other pool participants.

business_model.claim: Since 2023 (LR2, LR1, MR, Handy pools) and 2025 (Chemical-Handy and Chemical-MR pools), Hafnia's main pools operate as Disponent-Owner Pools, under which the company recognises gross revenue as principal for all vessels in those pools.
quotes: In 2023, we changed our LR2 Pool, LR1 Pool, MR Pool and Handy Pool from agent-to-owner pools to Disponent-Owner Pools
In 2025, we changed our Chemical-Handy Pool and Chemical-MR Pool to Disponent-Owner pools

We recognise gross revenue for all vessels employed in such Pools, in Revenue (Hafnia Vessels and TC Vessels) for our Hafnia Vessels and TC Vessels, and Revenue (External Vessels in Disponent-Owner Pools) for the External Vessels.

business_model.claim: Revenue is affected by hire/freight rates and the number of operating days, and is also affected by the mix of business between time charter, pool, and spot voyage charter employment.
quotes: Revenue is affected by hire/freight rates and the number of operating days a vessel operates.
Revenue is also affected by the mix of business between vessels on time charter, vessels in pools and vessels operating on voyage charter outside the pools.

business_model.claim: As at December 31, 2025, 74% of vessels in the Hafnia Fleet were operated in the spot market on short-term contracts normally not exceeding three months, making revenue highly sensitive to short-term rate fluctuations.
quotes: As at December 31, 2025, 74% of the vessels in our Hafnia Fleet were operated in the spot market on short-term contracts that normally do not extend beyond three months.

business_model.basis: stated in P3 (Item 5, Important Financial and Operational Terms)
business_model.claim: Under voyage charters, Hafnia bears all voyage expenses, which primarily include bunker fuel, port charges, canal tolls, cargo handling operations, and brokerage commissions.
quotes: Voyage expenses primarily include bunker and port expenses, as well as other voyage expenses such as canal tolls, cargo handling operations, brokerage commissions and the pool-allocated profit-sharing adjustment (pool allocation).
Under a voyage charter, we pay all voyage expenses.

business_model.basis: stated in P3 (Item 5, Important Financial and Operational Terms)
business_model.claim: Vessel operating expenses include crewing, repairs and maintenance, insurance, spares and consumable stores, lube oils, and communication; the three largest components are crewing, repairs and maintenance, and insurance.
quotes: Vessel operating expenses include crewing, repairs and maintenance, and insurance as well as other items such as spares and consumable stores, lube oils and communication.
The three largest components of our vessel operating expenses are crewing, repairs and maintenance and insurance expenses.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 risk factors and P3 MD&A; figures from F2 income statement
risks.claim: Hafnia's core earnings engine is in sharp decline: revenue fell from $2,868,647 (table in thousands) to $2,281,909 (table in thousands) and profit for the year fell from $774,035 (table in thousands) to $339,682 (table in thousands), while TCE income per operating day dropped from $33,000 to $25,205, driven by 74% of the Hafnia Fleet operating in the short-term spot market.
quotes: We are particularly exposed to the short-term spot market. As at December 31, 2025, 74% of the vessels in our Hafnia Fleet were operated in the spot market on short-term contracts that normally do not extend beyond three months.
The tanker industry is both cyclical and volatile in terms of charter rates and profitability.

risks.basis: Figures from F3 cash flow statement and F1 balance sheet; new credit facilities from P1

quotes: Net cash provided by operating activities | 602,889 | 1,030,364 | 1,060,806
Net (decrease)/increase in cash and cash equivalents | (90,993) | 61,047 | (57,804)

risks.basis: Stated in P2 risk factors; figures from F1 balance sheet and F2 income statement; compliance from P4
risks.claim: Hafnia carries total borrowings of $1,122,976 (table in thousands) ($910,402 non-current and $212,574 current), with interest expense of $49,768 (table in thousands) in 2025, and the risk factors warn that inability to service debt could result in loss of vessels.
quotes: We have a significant amount of financial debt and servicing our current or future indebtedness limits funds available for other purposes and if we cannot service our debt, we may lose the vessels in our Hafnia Fleet.

Our credit facilities and lease financing agreements contain covenants that may limit our ability to conduct certain activities, and further, we may be unable to comply with such covenants, which could result in an event of default under the terms of such agreements.

risks.basis: Stated in P1 (Investment in TORM section) and P2 (risk factors)
risks.claim: Hafnia committed $311.4 million to acquire 14,156,061 Class A Shares of TORM plc (approximately 13.97% of issued share capital) on December 22, 2025, with no assurance that a strategic combination will materialise.
quotes: We acquired and hold the TORM Class A Shares for investment purposes. We believe consolidation is positive for the tanker industry generally and are evaluating potential strategic opportunities involving the Investment in TORM, including a range of potential options for a combination of the two businesses.

There can be no assurance that TORM plc and we will pursue, enter or consummate a potential transaction and there are several risks associated with the negotiation, completion and timing of any potential transaction.

risks.claim: Geopolitical disruptions in the Red Sea, Strait of Hormuz, and US-China trade tensions, including new port fees and the America's Maritime Action Plan proposing universal import fees of 1 to 25 cents per kilogram on non-U.S.-built vessels, could adversely affect operations and charter rates.
quotes: Disruptions to shipping in the Red Sea, Arabian Gulf, and Strait of Hormuz in connection with the conflict between Israel and Hamas and the conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran or other disruptions to commonly used trading routes could have a negative effect on our operations, business, cash flows, financial condition, and results of operation.

In February 2026, the United States announced America's Maritime Action Plan according to which universal fees of between 1 to 25 cents per kilogram of cargo imported into the United States by non-U.S.-built vessels could be imposed.

risks.basis: Stated in P1 (vessel acquisitions and divestments, Recent Developments, and fleet strategy sections)
risks.claim: Hafnia is shrinking its owned fleet through divestments without offsetting acquisitions in the near term: in 2025 it divested four vessels and acquired none, and in the period from January 1, 2026 to the date of the Annual Report it divested six vessels and committed to sell six more, while newbuild deliveries are not expected before Q3 2028.
quotes: In 2025, we divested four vessels and we did not acquire any vessels (excluding the acquisition of vessels by the utilisation of purchase options in our sale and lease-back arrangements).

In the period from January 1, 2026 until the date of this Annual Report, we divested three LR1 vessels, two MR vessels, and one Handy vessel, and further committed to the sale of one LR1, two MRs, and three Handy vessels, all to external parties and pending delivery to the buyers. We have not acquired any vessels during the period

On April 3, 2026, we announced that we had signed a contract for the construction of eight MR newbuild product tankers from a South Korean shipyard, with a total purchase price of approximately US$405 million, with deliveries expected between the third quarter of 2028 and the second quarter of 2029.

risks.claim: The product tanker newbuild orderbook equalled approximately 18% of the existing world product tanker fleet in tonnage terms at the end of 2025, creating a risk of oversupply that could depress charter rates.
quotes: The product tanker newbuild orderbook equalled approximately 18% of the existing world product tanker fleet in tonnage terms at the end of 2025. No assurance can be given that the orderbook will not increase further in proportion to the existing fleet.

An oversupply of product tanker capacity or a decrease in demand for product tankers or the products carried by product tankers may render us unable to re-charter our Hafnia Vessels and TC Vessels at attractive rates.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 risk factors, citing IEA and OPEC forecasts
risks.claim: A shift in consumer demand away from oil towards renewable energy sources, and the potential occurrence of 'peak oil', could reduce long-term demand for product tanker capacity and adversely affect Hafnia's future performance.
quotes: A shift in or disruption of the consumer demand from oil towards other energy resources such as wind, solar energy and other renewable energy sources, electricity, natural gas, liquefied natural gas, or hydrogen as well as a shift in governmental commitments and support for energy transition programs will potentially negatively affect the demand for our product tankers.

The International Energy Agency forecasts under their current policies scenario that global oil demand will peak in 2050, but that in a stated policies scenario, the demand for oil will flatten around 2030.
